kind.description: Whether the subject sells a product or makes content. This decides who counts as a competitor: for a product subject, competitors are the **same kind of supply** a buyer would compare prices against; for a creator subject, competitors are **peers making the same kind of content**. These are different questions, and one yardstick for both is always wrong for one of them: an educational account is a real competitor for a creator subject but only a commentator on the category for a product subject. Defaults to creator, because discovery was historically tuned for creators.

caption_phrases.description: Content-form phrases from the creator's own captions, supplemented by canonical YouTube video titles, copied verbatim: do not rewrite, translate or polish them. Caption and title samples qualify independently; merge and deduplicate their phrases while preserving the original caption phrases and their order. Do not substitute descriptions or transcripts for captions. Search terms must land on these original words; subject.description is a description of the creator, and search terms derived from it retrieve 'people described this way' rather than 'people making the same kind of content'. Include only phrases that name a content format; leave out calls to action and demonstratives.

seed_content_ref.description: When the user starts account discovery from a public post, record its resolved canonical content_id. An empty string is invalid. The report must keep this starting point; the analysis window does not need to widen for it. Do not put the subject account in the comparison roster.

window_policy.description: How the primary competitor window was chosen. recent_30d is the default when omitted: last 30 days UTC. user_named_span is only for a span the user named. A research window is not an account-selection constraint.

requested_competitor_count.description: How many competitor accounts the Creator explicitly asked for (e.g. 10 for 'find 10 similar channels'). Omit when no number was named. It does not raise the per-run cap; the reply says so when the run compared fewer.
